text:
NARROWED FROM P1 TO P3 AND MOSTLY COVERED. m1 measured what I had only read.

THE PRODUCTION SEGMENTER OVER ALL TEN PARAPHRASES: Precise yields 2 units; EVERY OTHER PARAPHRASE YIELDS EXACTLY 1. So the merge branch is a NO-OP for nine of ten -- verified structurally: 'if recall.units.size == 1 then recall' returns the graph untouched.

MY TITLE WAS THE PROBLEM. 'The WOG alignment fixture overrides the production segmenter' reads as systemic. It applies to ONE paraphrase. I filed a P1 sized against the broader reading, and anyone picking it up would have scoped for a survey that does not exist.

ALREADY IN HAND, and stronger than what I asked for: new-engineer asked m1 to rule A/B inside slice E; m1 ruled A on that measurement; new-engineer applied it -- segmentOne renamed to an explicit statementAcceptanceRecall adapter, docs stating that copying statement targets onto clauses would INVENT EVIDENCE, and a capacity-to-fail law pinning THE COMPLETE DIVERGENCE VECTOR as exactly Vector(Precise -> 2). A law that pins the whole vector cannot silently grow a second case.

REMAINING: confirm the Precise annotation itself -- whether that one paraphrase's expectation should be stated per statement or per clause. That is a single annotation question, not an architecture question.
